title: Cloudflare, New Year 2017: The leap second and the negative duration

subtitle.simple: How a clock set back by one second made some websites impossible to find.
subtitle.tech: Leap second, non-monotonic wall clock, negative RTT, rand.Int63n panic in RRDNS.

sub.simple: finds the address for a name

headline.simple: Problem: On New Year's night 2017, some visitors could not find websites. Why?
headline.tech: Bug: RRDNS panic on CNAME lookups after the leap second on Jan 1, 2017.

text.simple: A visitor asks at which address shop.example.com can be found.
text.tech: A client asks RRDNS for a name that requires resolving a CNAME.

text.simple: The lookup draws lots to pick a helper; whoever was fast last time gets more tickets.
text.tech: Weighted random selection of the upstream based on measured RTTs.

text.simple: It checks the clock and notes the start time.
text.tech: start := time.Now() reads the wall clock, not a monotonic clock.

text.simple: Right now a leap second is added worldwide, and the clock is set back one second.
text.tech: Leap second 23:59:60 UTC: the wall clock jumps back 1 s; Go 1.7 has no monotonic time.

text.simple: The lookup asks helper A and has the address after three thousandths of a second.
text.tech: Upstream query, answer after 3 ms.

text.simple: The end time is now before the start time, so the question seems to have taken minus 997 milliseconds.
text.tech: rtt := time.Now().Sub(start) yields −997 ms; the code assumes this never happens.

text.simple: The lookup writes the impossible duration into the notebook, which gives helper A minus tickets.
text.tech: updateRTT accepts the value; the smoothed RTT and thus A's weight turn negative.

text.simple: This visitor still gets the address, but the error now sits in the notebook.
text.tech: The current request is still answered; the negative value stays stored.

text.simple: On the next question the lookup wants to draw again, but minus tickets make that impossible, and it gives up.
text.tech: rand.Int63n gets a negative argument and panics; recover catches it and the lookup fails.

text.simple: The visitor gets no address, and the website will not open.
text.tech: The client receives an error response; only CNAME lookups were affected.

headline.simple: Solution: A duration below zero is recognized as impossible and never written down.
headline.tech: Fix: Detect and discard a negative RTT before it reaches the weighting.

text.tech: A client asks RRDNS for a name that requires resolving a CNAME.

text.simple: The lookup draws lots to pick a helper; whoever was fast last time gets more tickets.
text.tech: Weighted random selection of the upstream based on measured RTTs.

text.simple: It checks the clock and notes the start time.

text.simple: The lookup asks helper A and has the address after three thousandths of a second.

text.simple: The end time is before the start time, but now the lookup knows a negative duration is impossible and throws it away.
text.tech: New: if rtt < 0, the measurement is discarded and updateRTT is not called.

text.simple: The notebook stays as it was: helper A keeps its tickets.
text.tech: The RTT stats stay unchanged, and all weights stay positive.

text.simple: The visitor gets the address.
text.tech: The request is answered normally.

text.simple: Stress test: The clock is still a second behind, but on the next question the tickets are right and the draw works.
text.tech: Even while the wall clock is shifted, rand.Int63n gets only positive weights.

text.simple: The lookup asks helper A and passes the address on to the visitor.
text.tech: Upstream query and response as usual.

text.simple: Result: Even on the night of the leap second, every visitor finds their website.
text.tech: Result: no panic; all CNAME lookups are answered.
